name: title
description: A short phrase or sentence describing the dataset. In many discovery systems, the title will be displayed in the results list from a search, and therefore should be human readable and reasonable to display in a list of such names. This attribute is also recommended by the NetCDF Users Guide(link is external) and the CF conventions(link is external).
comments: Provided in English

name: summary
description: A paragraph describing the dataset, analogous to an abstract for a paper.
comments: Provided in English

name: keywords
description: A comma-separated list of keywords and/or phrases. Keywords may be common words or phrases, terms from a controlled vocabulary.
comments:
If keywords are extracted from e.g. GCMD Science Keywords, add keywords_vocabulary='GCMDSK' and prefix in any case each keyword with the appropriate prefix. 
See Note on keywords and examples below.
requirements:
Required. 
At least one keyword from the GCMD Science keyword vocabulary is required

name: keywords_vocabulary
description: If you are using a controlled vocabulary for the words/phrases in your "keywords" attribute, this is the unique name or identifier of the vocabulary from which keywords are taken. If more than one keyword vocabulary is used, each may be presented with a prefix and a following comma, so that keywords may optionally be prefixed with the controlled vocabulary key.
comments:
If more than one keyword vocabulary is used, each may be presented with a prefix and a following comma. Ex: ‘GCMDSK:GCMD Science Keywords, ..’ Keywords should in this case be prefixed with the appropriate controlled vocabulary key. When keywords_vocabulary is not specified the default value of None will be used. 
See Note on keywords and examples below.
requirements:
Required. 
At least for GCMD Science Keyword vocabulary

name: geospatial_lat_min
description: Describes a simple lower latitude limit; may be part of a 2- or 3-dimensional bounding region. Geospatial_lat_min specifies the southernmost latitude covered by the dataset. Must be decimal degrees north.
comments:
Use at least 2 decimals.
This must be decimal degrees north.
See Note on geospatial extent below.

name: geospatial_lat_max
description: Describes a simple upper latitude limit; may be part of a 2- or 3-dimensional bounding region. Geospatial_lat_max specifies the northernmost latitude covered by the dataset. Must be decimal degrees north.
comments:
Use at least 2 decimals.
This must be decimal degrees north.
See Note on geospatial extent below.

name: geospatial_lon_min
description: Describes a simple longitude limit; may be part of a 2- or 3-dimensional bounding region. geospatial_lon_min specifies the westernmost longitude covered by the dataset. See also geospatial_lon_max. Must be decimal degrees east (negative westwards).
comments:
Use at least 2 decimals.
This must be decimal degrees east (negative westwards).
See Note on geospatial extent below.

name: geospatial_lon_max
description: Describes a simple longitude limit; may be part of a 2- or 3-dimensional bounding region. geospatial_lon_max specifies the easternmost longitude covered by the dataset. Must be decimal degrees east (negative westwards).
comments:
Use at least 2 decimals.
This must be decimal degrees east (negative westwards).
See Note on geospatial extent below.

name: time_coverage_start
description: Describes the time of the first data point in the data set. Use the ISO 8601:2004 date format, preferably the extended format as recommended in the Attribute Content Guidance section. I.e. YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (always use UTC).

name: time_coverage_end
description: Describes the time of the last data point in the data set. Use ISO 8601:2004 date format, preferably the extended format as recommended in the Attribute Content Guidance section. I.e. YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (always use UTC).
comments: If the file is being appended with new data, this can be left out and the dataset will then be considered an ongoing effort.

name: date_created
description: The date on which this version of the data was created. (Modification of values implies a new version, hence this would be assigned the date of the most recent values modification.) Metadata changes are not considered when assigning the date_created. The ISO 8601:2004 extended date format is recommended, as described in the Attribute Content Guidance section. E.g. 2020-10-20T12:35:00Z.
comments: If date_created is not provided, a default current datetime stamp will be generated.

name: license
description: Provide the URL and identifier to a standard license. It is strongly recommended to use identifiers and URL's from https://spdx.org/licenses/(link is external) and to use a form similar to <URL> (<Identifier>) using elements from the SPDX source listed above.
comments:
The recommended way to provide this information is license: "http://spdx.org/licenses/CC-BY-4.0(link is external) (CC-BY-4.0)" 
If a standard license cannot be parsed this field will be extracted into free text. 
See the Note on license below.

name: creator_type
description: Specifies the type of creator with one of the following: 'person', 'group', 'institution', or 'position'. If this attribute is not specified, the creator is assumed to be a person.
comments:
Do not use ',' except for separating elements. Use this for principal Investigator. Consistency across comma separated lists for all creator_* attributes are required. 
See Note about creators and examples below

name: creator_name
description: The name of the person (or other creator type specified by the creator_type attribute) principally responsible for creating this data.
comments: See creator_type for more information.

name: creator_institution
description: The institution of the creator; should uniquely identify the creator's institution.
comments:
This attribute's value should be specified even if it matches the value of publisher_institution, or if creator_type is institution. 
Please use only long names for this field.
See creator_type for more information.

name: creator_email
description: The email address of the person (or other creator type specified by the creator_type attribute) principally responsible for creating this data.
comments:
Please use institutional emails when possible. 
See creator_type for more information.

name: publisher_name
description: It specifies the name of the publisher.
comments:
This is the name of the data center publishing the data. The recommended form is “long name (short name)” 
For data hosted by MET see the recommended values in the Note on publisher and example below.

name: publisher_url
description: The URL of the publisher.
comments: For data hosted by MET see the recommended values in the Note on publisher and example below.

name: publisher_institution
description: It specifies the institution of the publisher.
comments:
This is the name of the institution publishing the data. For a publisher of type "institution" this is often the same as publisher_name. 
For data hosted by MET see the recommended values in the Note on publisher and example below.

name: publisher_email
description: The email of the publisher or publisher contact.
comments: For data hosted by MET see the recommended values in the Note on publisher and example below.

name: project
description: The name of the project(s) principally responsible for originating this data.
comments:
Multiple projects can be separated by commas, as described under Attribute Content Guidelines. Examples: 'PATMOS-X', 'Extended Continental Shelf Project'. If each sub-string includes a keyword in parentheses, the content within the parentheses is interpreted as the short name for the project while the rest is the long name. E.g. 'Nansen Legacy (NLEG)'. 
See Note on project and example below
